title: TCA overdose and gastric lavage
stem: Resus 2. A 40-year-old woman on treatment for depression was found drowsy at home by her husband, who had left her an hour earlier. An empty packet of amitriptyline 25 mg (60 tablets) was beside her. GCS E2 V2 M4, HR 128, BP 84/46, RR 10, SpO2 91% on room air.

review.text: Gastric lavage window. Your notes extend lavage to about 4 hours for anticholinergic drugs. That is a local HK practice point. International guidance (AACT/EAPCCT) says lavage is not routine: only for a potentially life-threatening ingestion, ideally within 1 hour, with a protected airway and an experienced operator.

notes:
Checked against TOXBASE, the Hong Kong Poison Information Centre (HKPIC) guidance, and the AACT/EAPCCT position papers on gastric lavage (2013) and activated charcoal.

Tricyclics block fast sodium channels (broad QRS, VT), alpha receptors (hypotension), muscarinic receptors (tachycardia, dilated pupils, retention, delayed gastric emptying) and cause seizures. QRS over 100 ms predicts seizures; over 160 ms predicts arrhythmias. A terminal R wave in aVR over 3 mm is another marker.

Treatment: airway (intubate for a falling GCS; avoid hypoventilation and acidosis), sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 1–2 mmol/kg (50–100 mL) boluses for QRS over 100 ms, hypotension or arrhythmia, aiming for pH 7.45–7.55; benzodiazepines for seizures (not phenytoin); fluids then noradrenaline for hypotension; lipid emulsion and prolonged CPR in arrest. Avoid flumazenil and class Ia/Ic antiarrhythmics; physostigmine is contraindicated.

Decontamination: activated charcoal 50 g if within 1 hour and the airway is safe (via the tube once intubated). Gastric lavage is not routine (AACT/EAPCCT): consider it only for a potentially life-threatening ingestion, ideally within 1 hour, with a protected airway, by someone experienced. Your notes argue for lavage in exactly that setting and extend the window for anticholinergic drugs (up to about 4 hours); that is a local HK practice point, not an international recommendation. The steps in your notes (left lateral, head down, 36–40 Fr tube, measured, confirmed, 200–250 mL warm aliquots until clear, save aspirate) are correct.

ABCDE.mark: Recognises an unprotected airway and hypoventilation

ABCDE.r: Pupils 6 mm, dry flushed skin, palpable bladder, quiet bowel sounds.

ECG.r: Sinus tachycardia, QRS 150 ms, prolonged QT, tall terminal R wave in aVR.
ECG.mark: Identifies sodium-channel blockade: broad QRS and terminal R in aVR

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Bicarbonate for the broad QRS; benzodiazepine ready for seizures.

opts.t: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 100 mL (1–2 mmol/kg) IV now; repeat to narrow the QRS, target pH 7.45–7.55
opts.mark: Sodium bicarbonate for QRS over 100 ms and hypotension

opts.t: Lorazepam or diazepam drawn up for seizures
Fluid bolus; noradrenaline if still hypotensive
Flumazenil in case of benzodiazepines too
opts.r: Flumazenil can precipitate seizures and arrhythmias in TCA overdose.
Phenytoin blocks sodium channels too and can worsen cardiotoxicity. Benzodiazepines only.
Contraindicated in TCA poisoning: asystole has occurred.

steps.label: Airway
steps.hint: GCS 8 with hypoventilation: RSI, and avoid acidosis after intubation.

opts.t: RSI now; after intubation ventilate a little faster to avoid acidosis (pH 7.45–7.55)

steps.label: Decontamination
steps.hint: Airway protected, within about an hour, potentially lethal dose: lavage is considered. Left lateral, head down, measured large tube, warm aliquots, charcoal after.

opts.t: Confirm the indication: life-threatening dose, early, airway protected; no caustic or sharp objects
Left lateral, head down; strong suction ready
Measure a 36–40 Fr orogastric tube from the mouth to the epigastrium; lubricate
Insert; confirm position (aspirate and pH, or air insufflation)
Aspirate the stomach and save a sample for toxicology
Warm fluid 200–250 mL at a time by gravity; drain; repeat until clear
Instil activated charcoal 50 g down the tube, then clamp and withdraw
opts.mark: Activated charcoal after lavage; clamps before withdrawal

opts.t: Lavage the unintubated drowsy patient in the sitting position
opts.r: Unprotected airway: aspiration. Never without a protected airway.

opts.t: Force a litre in quickly with a syringe
opts.r: Large volumes push drug through the pylorus and cause aspiration and electrolyte problems.

steps.label: Phone
steps.hint: Poison centre and ICU; psychiatric assessment once recovered.

opts.t: Hong Kong Poison Information Centre / TOXBASE for advice
ICU: intubated TCA overdose, QRS narrowing with bicarbonate
Mental health assessment when medically fit

qs.q: QRS duration that predicts seizures in TCA poisoning?

qs.a: Not routine; life-threat and protected airway only
wrong: Routine for every overdose presenting within 4 hours of ingestion
Safe without a protected airway if awake

qs.q: Why may the stomach still hold tablets after an hour?
wrong: TCAs are never absorbed from the stomach, only the colon
Charcoal slows the absorption of tablets

rules.fail: Lavage before the airway was protected.

badge.name: Salt of the Earth
badge.flavor: Broad QRS? Bicarbonate. Airway before the tube in the stomach.

cards.q: First drug for TCA overdose with QRS 140 ms and hypotension?
cards.why: Sodium load and alkalinisation reverse sodium-channel blockade.

cards.q: ECG sign in aVR suggesting sodium-channel blockade?
options: A deep Q wave over 3 mm

cards.q: Gastric lavage tube size in adults?
cards.why: Large bore to pass tablet fragments.
Keeps the pylorus up and reduces aspiration.

cards.q: Activated charcoal is most useful within…
cards.why: Later use may be considered for delayed-release or anticholinergic drugs.
